strength.warning.keyboard_row: Rows of keys like “qwertz” are easy to guess.
strength.warning.keyboard_pattern: Short keyboard patterns are easy to guess.
strength.warning.repeated_chars: Repeats like “aaa” are easy to guess.
strength.warning.repeated_pattern: Repeats like “abcabc” are only slightly harder to guess.
strength.warning.top_password: This is one of the most common passwords.
strength.warning.similar_to_common: This is similar to a commonly used password.
strength.warning.sequence: Sequences like “abc” or “6543” are easy to guess.
strength.warning.single_word: A word by itself is easy to guess.
strength.warning.name: Names are easy to guess, especially your own.
strength.warning.common_name: Common names and surnames are easy to guess.
strength.suggestion.use_words: Use a few random words and avoid common phrases.
strength.suggestion.no_symbols_needed: No need for symbols, digits or capital letters.
strength.suggestion.add_words: Add another word or two. Uncommon words are better.
strength.suggestion.capitalization: Capital letters don't help very much.
strength.suggestion.all_uppercase: All capitals are almost as easy to guess as all lowercase.
strength.suggestion.reversed: Reversed words aren't much harder to guess.
strength.suggestion.substitutions: Predictable substitutions like “@” for “a” don't help much.
strength.suggestion.longer_keyboard_patt: Use a longer keyboard pattern with more turns.
strength.suggestion.avoid_personal_years: Avoid years that are associated with you.
strength.suggestion.avoid_personal_dates: Avoid dates and years that are associated with you.
totp.problem.one_time_code: This is a single code, not the setup key. Codes change every 30 seconds. You need the key the website shows when you set up two-factor authentication (often under “Can't scan the QR code?”).
totp.problem.invalid: This setup key is not valid. It usually has 16 to 32 letters and digits, for example JBSW Y3DP EHPK 3PXP.
error.network: The server could not be reached. Check your connection.
error.wrongMasterPassword: Wrong master password. Check upper and lower case and Caps Lock.
error.invalidCredentials: The email, master password or Secret Key is incorrect. Your Secret Key is in your Emergency Kit.
error.invalidSecretKey: This doesn't look like a Secret Key. It starts with P1- and has 26 more characters.
error.rateLimited: Too many sign-in attempts. Try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. If this wasn't you, someone may be guessing – your Secret Key keeps the account safe.
error.conflict: This item was changed on another device. The latest version has been loaded.
notice.preview: Passbox is in early development and has not been independently audited. Don't store secrets you can't afford to lose yet.
twoFactor.title: Confirm it's you
twoFactor.description: Your account is protected with two-factor sign-in. Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.descriptionKey: Your account is protected with two-factor sign-in. Use your security key or enter a recovery code.
twoFactor.useCode: Use a code from the app instead
twoFactor.keyWaiting: Touch your security key or confirm on this device …
twoFactor.keyFailed: The security key was not accepted or the request was cancelled. Try again or use a recovery code.
twoFactor.keyUnavailable: Your security key works in the Passbox web app. Here, enter a recovery code.
twoFactor.rememberHint: No code is needed here for 30 days. Only choose this on your own device.
twoFactor.recoveryUsed: Recovery code used. {count, plural, =0 {No codes left – create new ones in Settings.} one {# code left.} other {# codes left.}}
error.invalidTwoFactorCode: That code isn't correct. App codes change every 30 seconds – enter the current one.
error.twoFactorExpired: The sign-in took too long. Enter your master password again.
